clue.text: Beneficial to get two-thirds cut in pay ?

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the word for pay

parts.note: pay means salary

indicators.note: two-thirds of a three-letter word keeps two of its letters, here its last two

explanation.surface: Someone is told a pay cut of two-thirds will do them good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds' of CUT is UT, which goes 'in' SALARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something salutary is wholesome and does good, so it is beneficial.

clue.text: A pair of shorts and a long foot

definitions.text: A pair of shorts and a long foot

parts.words: A pair of shorts and a long foot
parts.note: in verse a foot is a unit of metre; this one has two short syllables followed by a long one

explanation.walkthrough: 'shorts' looks like trousers and 'foot' like the body part; both are terms of prosody.
explanation.definitionFit: This metrical foot is defined as two short syllables then a stressed long one.

clue.text: Wasteful use of foreign article-—funny carry-on !.

parts.note: une is the French indefinite article

indicators.note: funny carries the next word, holding it inside itself

parts.note: funny means comical
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint about the waste of some foreign item and the fuss it causes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry-on' reads as a fuss, but it splits: 'carry' is the container signal and 'on' is the piece carried inside the word for funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uneconomical means using more resources than needed, which is wasteful.

clue.text: Medicine for the love-sick ?

parts.note: split the remedy word as anti plus dote: something against doting, i.e. against being infatuated

explanation.walkthrough: The word for a remedy splits into ANTI (against) and DOTE (be infatuated), so it reads as a cure for doting lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote counters a poison, a medicine in the clue's sense.

clue.text: The pirate's last supporter?

parts.note: pirates were traditionally hanged from a spar on a ship's mast, the last thing ever to hold them up

explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a friend or ally; it is the spar from which pirates were hanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is the outer end of a ship's yard, the spar used for hangings at sea.

clue.text: Birds used to be seen round Russian mount

indicators.note: round says the past-tense word goes around the other piece

parts.note: used to be means was

indicators.note: in a down clue mount means climb, so the word read upwards is reversed

parts.note: red is a long-standing label for a Russian, from the Soviet era

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers spot birds circling a mountain in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' in a down clue means read upwards; 'round' wraps the past-tense word around that reversed colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Waders are long-legged shore birds such as herons and sandpipers.

clue.text: Charles turns up with a one pound note

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the whole string from the bottom, so it is reversed

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A man named Charles arrives carrying a one-pound banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: A, I, L, E together read upwards ('turns up'). Charles Lamb wrote essays as Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: The essayist Charles Lamb used this pen name for his Essays.

clue.text: Many such drivers couldn't

parts.note: many such motorists show no concern, and the word for them follows that phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The clue ends on 'couldn't'; add 'care less' and the adjective for reckless motorists appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless driver pays too little attention, and couldn't care less.

clue.text: Girl sees another following a horse

indicators.note: following puts the second girl's name after the horse

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
another girl, Ella

explanation.surface: A girl watches a friend riding behind a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sees' is a link; 'following' puts the second girl's name after the horse breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabella is a female forename.

clue.text: Merchandise said to be clothes

indicators.note: said to be signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: clothes are wear, as in menswear

explanation.definitionFit: Ware means goods for sale, as in hardware or wares.

clue.text: Social work done by Dr Hill — a few repairs in church

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: repairs means the letters are fixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor does some social work by mending a few things in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: DRHILLAFEW 'repairs' to HILDWELFAR, put 'in' CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Child welfare is the branch of social services looking after children.

clue.text: Pays for bottle of his mixture-a pound

indicators.note: mixture means the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pays a pound for a bottle of a man's mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLEOFHIS, in a 'mixture', gives FOOTSTHEBIL; add L.
explanation.definitionFit: To foot the bill is the idiom for paying the cost.

clue.text: Slowly encircles a building

indicators.note: encircles says the tempo word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly

explanation.surface: Something slowly circles round a building.
explanation.walkthrough: LENTO 'encircles' A. The 'a' belongs to the wordplay, so the definition is just 'building'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed or extension built against a wall.

clue.text: Press one roughly, for an answer

indicators.note: roughly means the letters are handled loosely and rearranged

explanation.surface: Push a button firmly to reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply, which is an answer.

clue.text: Walked stiffly out ?

definitions.meaning: to walk heavily and stiffly, clumping along
in cricket a batsman is out this way when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while he is out of his ground

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: being stumped is a way of being dismissed, or 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumping is heavy plodding walking, and also a cricket dismissal.

clue.text: Grounds not drained with the rest?

definitions.text: Grounds not drained with the rest?

parts.words: Grounds not drained with the rest
parts.note: coffee grounds are what stays behind in the cup or pot when the liquid is poured off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' suggests land; it is coffee dregs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid, like dregs.

clue.text: Stellar distances bring equality with sex, say

parts.note: par means equality, as in on a par

indicators.note: say signals a word that sounds like the clue word

parts.note: the clue word sex, spoken

explanation.surface: A remark about how far gender equality has to go.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR, then 'say' turns SEX into the sound-alike SECS.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is an astronomical unit of length, about 3.26 light years.

clue.text: Like Biblical character, has a way of mounting attacks

parts.note: like means as
Saul is the first king of Israel in the Bible

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means going up, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Like a Bible figure, someone has a way of launching attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; 'mounting' turns the street abbreviation upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaults are violent attacks.

clue.text: Garment charged by mistake ?

definitions.meaning: a knitted jacket fastened down the front
the earl who led the Light Brigade in its mistaken charge at Balaclava in 1854

explanation.walkthrough: The Charge of the Light Brigade, led by Lord Cardigan, came from a misunderstood order; the jacket is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted button-up jacket and the earl it is named after both carry this name.

clue.text: Fielding character shot in America?

definitions.meaning: Squire ... is a character in Henry Fielding's novel Tom Jones
a cowboy film, shot on location in the American West

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fielding' looks like cricket; it is the novelist Henry Fielding.
explanation.definitionFit: A squire in Tom Jones and a genre of cowboy movie share the name.

clue.text: Trained obedience lacking in this follower

indicators.note: lacking says a piece is taken away from the word for trained obedience

parts.note: discipline is trained obedience

explanation.surface: This follower's training never instilled obedience.
explanation.walkthrough: DISCIPLINE 'lacking' IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple follows a teacher.

clue.text: Robber raised rent 'at the quarter

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
E, east, is one of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: A thief puts the rent up when it is due at quarter day.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP 'raised' is PIR; add AT and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a robber at sea.

clue.text: A gunner has returned the waste

indicators.note: returned means the whole run of letters comes back the other way

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: A soldier has come back from the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: A, RA and HAS read backwards ('returned').
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahara is the vast desert of North Africa, a waste of sand.

clue.text: Fish might be well floured ?

parts.note: a small freshwater fish named after a flour-grinder's digit, which might well be covered in flour

explanation.walkthrough: The fish's name belongs to a person who grinds corn, whose thumb, used to test flour, would be well floured.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullhead fish is also called this, after a flour-grinder's flattened thumb.

clue.text: Musical instrument in fairly recent use

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that has come into use quite recently.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across fairLY REcent.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is an ancient stringed instrument, like a small harp.

clue.text: A churchman's middle finger

indicators.note: middle takes the inside of the word, all but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A clergyman makes a rude gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: W. R. Inge was Dean of St Paul's.
explanation.definitionFit: Dean Inge was a well-known Anglican cleric and writer.

clue.text: He tells of island retreat to the right

indicators.note: retreat means go back, so the island name is reversed

parts.note: Arran is a Scottish island
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A man recounts a retreat across an island, going to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: ARRAN 'retreat' gives NARRA, then TO and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator is the one who tells a story.

clue.text: Bird sent *mixed fish

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A bird is sent a mixed assortment of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a young bird not yet out of the nest.
